title: Sufficient in a Dish, Not Required

scenes.tts: A kidney cell line does not form synapses. Yet make it produce one neuronal protein, called neuroligin, and axons that touch it in a dish act as if they had found a partner. What do those axons do? And does the brain need neuroligin to do the same? Each contact in the brain has to say what kind of synapse it will become.
scenes.visual: A bare kidney cell sits in the dish; an axon grows across it; yellow neuroligin stubs appear on the cell; a question mark waits at the contact.
scenes.narration: A kidney cell line does not form synapses. Yet make it produce one neuronal protein, called neuroligin, and axons that touch it in a dish act as if they had found a partner. What do those axons do? And does the brain need neuroligin to do the same? Each contact in the brain has to say what kind of synapse it will become.

scenes.tts: Grow kidney cells under axons. Where an axon crosses a cell that makes neuroligin, synaptic vesicles gather at the contact. Where it crosses other cells, they do not. The axon also releases those vesicles and takes them back. A dye taken up during release marks the working terminals, so the cluster is more than a pile of parts.
scenes.visual: A control cell and a neuroligin cell under one axon; vesicle dots gather only over the neuroligin cell, then hop out to the contact and back.
scenes.caption: Grow kidney cells under axons. Where an axon crosses a cell that makes neuroligin, synaptic vesicles gather at the contact. Where it crosses other cells, they do not. The axon also releases those vesicles and takes them back. A dye taken up during release marks the working terminals, so the cluster is more than a pile of parts.

scenes.tts: Neurexins sit on the axon side. Neuroligins are their partners on the other side. Now add soluble neurexin to the dish. It binds neuroligin first, so the axon's own neurexin cannot reach it. The vesicle clusters are blocked. So the effect runs through the bond between neurexin and neuroligin.
scenes.visual: Blue neurexin stubs on the axon clasp the yellow stubs; free blue neurexin caps the yellow stubs, the axon's stubs fade, and the vesicle cluster scatters.
scenes.narration: Neurexins sit on the axon side. Neuroligins are their partners on the other side. Now add soluble neurexin to the dish. It binds neuroligin first, so the axon's own neurexin cannot reach it. The vesicle clusters are blocked. So the effect runs through the bond between neurexin and neuroligin.

scenes.tts: So neuroligin can do this, on a kidney cell, in a dish. Call that sufficient. It is a clean test of one protein. But a dish tests what one protein can do. It does not test what the brain depends on. For that, you need a genetic experiment: take the protein away from the mouse and look at the synapses.
scenes.visual: The dish shrinks to the left, labelled sufficient; a dashed box with a question mark opens on the right, labelled required in the animal.
scenes.narration: So neuroligin can do this, on a kidney cell, in a dish. Call that sufficient. It is a clean test of one protein. But a dish tests what one protein can do. It does not test what the brain depends on. For that, you need a genetic experiment: take the protein away from the mouse and look at the synapses.

scenes.tts: Mice lacking neuroligins one, two and three were reported to have synapses in normal number and structure in the brainstem. But transmission was impaired, and the mice died from failed breathing. Mice lacking all three alpha-neurexins died soon after birth. Excitatory synapses were close to normal, inhibitory fewer, yet released transmitter poorly. Synapses formed. They worked badly.
scenes.visual: Two bar pairs, synapse number and transmission, wild type against knockout: number stays level, transmission drops; the heading then switches from neuroligin to neurexin mice.

scenes.tts: So alpha-neurexins and neuroligins are needed for normal synapse function and maturation, not for forming most synapses. Many organizers overlap. A dish with one organizer on a kidney cell tests what that one can do. Keep the rule. Sufficient in a dish is not the same as required in the animal.
scenes.visual: Two arrows leave neurexin and neuroligin: one to function and maturation (kept), one to forming most synapses (crossed out); then overlapping circles of organizers with only one lit in the dish; the rule appears.
